text: Anu, also called Ana and Danu, is an Irish goddess. Two identical rounded hills rise in southwestern Ireland. Prehistoric cairns cap them. They look like the nipples of the great mother goddess. The hills are called Da Chich Danann, which is translated as the Paps of Danu. People named the hills after a goddess Anu, of whom little is known. No story describes this supposed goddess of abundance. The early glossarist Cormac lists her as the mother of the gods of Ireland. Many scholars hold her identical to Danu, the purported ancestor of the Tuatha De Danann. Others argue she is a separate goddess of Ireland's abundance. Still others link her to Aine of Limerick or to Black Annis of Britain. In Christian times she merged with Saint Anne, the grandmother of Jesus. Many holy wells are dedicated to Saint Anne.
